operations.summary: Generate a package from a spec
operations.description:
Stateless generation: nothing is stored. Returns the full generated
package as files. Works without an API key: anonymous calls generate
the first 25 operations, rate limited per IP address, and the
response's `limits` object says what was held back and where to lift
it; anonymous calls from a spec URL also carry `claim.url`, a link
that turns the run into a project once a person signs in. With a key, the free plan generates the first 25 operations and
paid plans generate the whole spec. A present but invalid key is a
401, not a downgrade to anonymous.

spec.description: The specification for stateless generation, provided as exactly one URL or inline document.

url.description:
URL of an OpenAPI document, a GraphQL SDL file, or a GraphQL
endpoint (introspected automatically). Fetched server-side.

headers.description: Request headers for a protected URL. Sent on the document GET and GraphQL introspection POST, never returned or retained by stateless generation.

inline.description: Raw spec text (OpenAPI JSON/YAML or GraphQL SDL). Up to 10MB.

outputs.description: The one output package to generate. Linked projects can select any combination of outputs and keep each package current.

items.description: One customer-selected output. CLI and MCP include the private TypeScript request runtime they need; that dependency is not a selected or billable TypeScript SDK.

package_name.description: Registry name for the selected delivery package: an npm package, Python distribution, or Go module path. Defaults to a name derived from the API title.

config.description: Everything typeship needs beyond the spec, in one object: generation customization (globals, retries, pagination) and how the generated tooling behaves (cli, mcp, package, docs_url). Plain configuration. typeship never requires vendor extensions inside the spec itself. The same shape is accepted on a project and on POST /generate.

globals.description: Wire names of query/header parameters that become settable once on the generated client and auto-apply to every operation that accepts them; per-call values win. Names that match nothing are reported as generation warnings.

retries.description: Retry behavior. Top-level fields adjust every operation; operations maps operationId or "METHOD /path" keys to per-operation overrides.

pagination.description: Per-operation pagination control, keyed by operationId or "METHOD /path". Unmatched keys are reported as generation warnings.

items_field.description: Response field holding the item array.

anyOf.description: false disables pagination detection for the operation.

graphql.description: What a GraphQL schema cannot say about itself. Ignored for OpenAPI specs.

endpoint.description: The URL every request is POSTed to; the generated client's default baseUrl. Defaults to the URL the schema was fetched from. Without either, baseUrl is a required client option.

environments.description: Named endpoints (sandbox, production). Each becomes a client environment; the first is the default unless endpoint is set.

auth.description: How requests authenticate. bearer sends Authorization: Bearer; basic is for key-pair APIs (public key as username, private key as password); api_key sends a header named by api_key_header; none generates no auth option.

api_key_header.description: Header carrying the key when auth is api_key. Required for that mode; Typeship does not invent a vendor-specific header name.

title.description: The API's name; drives the package and client names ("Braintree" gives braintree and BraintreeClient). Defaults to a name derived from the endpoint's host.

scalars.description: JSON representation of each custom scalar, keyed by GraphQL scalar name. Unmapped scalars generate as the language's untyped JSON value and produce a warning. Unmatched keys warn.

cli.description: How the generated CLI behaves. Part of Config.

whoami_operation.description: resource.method of a zero-argument GET that the generated CLI's whoami command calls. Overrides auto-detection; a value that matches nothing is reported as a generation warning.

oauth_client_id.description: OAuth client id baked into the generated CLI for device-flow login. Without it, login prompts for a pasted credential.

oauth_scopes.description: Scopes requested during device-flow login. Include offline_access if the authorization server gates refresh tokens behind it.

oauth_audience.description: Audience sent with the device-authorization request, for authorization servers that require one to issue API-valid access tokens.

update_notice.description: Opt in to a once-a-day registry check that prints an upgrade hint. Off by default; generated code phones nobody unless this is enabled.

support_url.description: Where the generated CLI's feedback command sends users. GitHub issues/new URLs get a prefilled title and environment details.

auth_url.description: Base URL of the browser-approval endpoint pair used by CLI login. The CLI keeps the verifier and receives the credential directly; no key is pasted through a conversation.

mcp_url.description: Hosted MCP endpoint installed by the generated CLI instead of launching the package's local stdio server.

skills_repo.description: GitHub owner/name of the skills package the generated CLI offers to install during init.

mcp.description: How the generated MCP server and the hosted endpoint behave. Part of Config.

tool_mode.description: MCP tool shape. meta collapses per-operation tools into search_docs, read_docs, and execute so large APIs don't flood an agent's context window. Auto considers the serialized tool schemas, switching near 10k tokens or above 100 operations.

instructions.description: Guidance appended to the MCP server's instructions, which agents read once when they connect (server/discover): what to call first, conventions the spec does not state, what not to do. Carried by the package's server and the hosted endpoint alike.

tool_descriptions.description: Hand-written MCP tool descriptions keyed by operationId or "METHOD /path". Each replaces the text typeship derives for that operation (summary, first sentence, method and path, deprecation and auth notes). For flows the spec cannot describe, such as a multi-step upload. Keys that match no operation are reported as generation warnings.

package.description: Published-package metadata the API spec does not own. Repository is derived from each destination; release versions belong to packages.

version.description: Lockstep version fallback. Prefer packages.<output>.version so every SDK, CLI, and MCP package can advance independently.

license.description: SPDX identifier written into registry metadata. Defaults to info.license.

license_text.description: Exact LICENSE file contents. Supply this for licences the engine does not build in; MIT is built in when copyright is also set.

copyright.description: Copyright line used in generated license files.

bin_name.description: CLI executable name when it differs from the npm package name.

go_package_name.description: Go identifier when the destination repository name is unsuitable.

mcp_name.description: Official MCP registry name written into package.json.

docs_url.description: The API's documentation site. Read through its llms.txt by the generated CLI's docs command, the MCP server's docs tools, and the package's AGENTS.md. Defaults to the spec's externalDocs URL.

path.description: Repo-relative path inside the generated package.

converted.description: True when the input was Swagger 2.0 and was converted.

outputs.description: Customer-selected outputs present in this delivery package.

items.description: One customer-selected output. CLI and MCP include the private TypeScript request runtime they need; that dependency is not a selected or billable TypeScript SDK.

omitted_operation_count.description: Operations beyond the plan's endpoint allowance, not generated.

pr_url.description: Pull request opened by this regeneration, when one was.

pr_status.description: Whether a destination pull request opened, was unnecessary because the generated tree already matched, or could not be opened.

pr_error.description: Why the configured destination pull request was not opened. Generation itself still succeeded; fix this action and regenerate.

changelog.description: Markdown changelog entry for this regeneration, from the API surface diff. Absent on a first generation or when nothing changed.

breaking_count.description: Breaking changes in the diff; removed methods and fields, changed types, inputs that became required.

baseline.description: What the diff was measured against; "destination" means the .typeship/surface.json merged in the destination repository.

package_compatibility.description: The package compatibility verdict on the regeneration pull request; failure means breaking changes without a major version bump.

package_compatibility_note.description: The verdict in one line, as the commit status describes it.

previous_version.description: The package version the destination had before this regeneration.

limits.description: Present when the generation was capped: by the free plan, or because the call was anonymous. Absent on uncapped generations.

max_operations.description: How many operations this generation was allowed to include.

generated_operations.description: How many operations are present in the generated package.

omitted_operations.description: How many operations in the spec were left out.

total_operations.description: How many operations Typeship found in the complete specification.

signup_url.description: Anonymous calls only. Where to create an account.

claim.description: Anonymous, URL-sourced generations only. A link a signed-in person can open to turn this run into a project in their organization (same spec, outputs, and config). Lasts seven days. Null for inline specs; absent on keyed calls.

limit.description: Maximum number of resources to return. Default: 20.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the preceding page's next_cursor.

source.description: The single source of truth for where a project's specification lives.

headers_configured.description: Whether Typeship has stored write-only request headers for this URL.

auto_regen.description: Regenerate when the spec changes: on every push to the default branch for a repository source, ever…

nextPage.description: Arguments that fetch the next page; pass them to this tool

truncated.description: Present when the page was cut to fit the result size cap: how many items were omitted and how to ge…

operations.description: Stores a URL- or GitHub-sourced project. Free includes one stored project, every selected output, and the first 25 operations, while keeping manual and automatic regeneration, history, destination pull requests, and preview checks. Stateless POST /generate does not consume this slot. Pro adds projects and the whole spec.

Idempotency-Key.description: Uniquely identifies this creation attempt. Retrying the same request with the same key returns the original response instead of creating another project. Reusing a key with different parameters returns 409.

url.description: URL of an OpenAPI document, GraphQL SDL file, or GraphQL endpoint.

headers.description: Request headers for a protected URL. Values are never returned or recorded in revision history. When updating the same URL, omit headers to preserve the stored values or pass null to remove them. Changing the URL without headers clears the old values so a credential is never forwarded to a different source.

operations.summary: Generate outputs and open pull requests
operations.description:
Resolves the project's URL or GitHub source, generates every
configured delivery package, stores each result in the project's history,
and attempts to open a pull request in every configured destination.
When the complete generated tree already matches a destination, no
commit, branch, or pull request is created and that generation reports
`pr_status: no_changes`. This is the same pipeline automatic
regeneration runs after a source change.
